# The resolved dependency set — every package that ends up in the image, at the
# exact version, including the ones nothing asks for directly.
#
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# THIS FILE IS GENERATED. Do not hand-edit it.
#
#     docker run --rm -v "$PWD/requirements.txt:/req.txt:ro" python:3.13-slim \
#         sh -c 'pip install -q -r /req.txt && pip freeze --exclude-editable'
#
# Regenerate it whenever requirements.txt changes, and read the diff before
# committing — an unexpected package appearing is exactly what this exists to
# make visible.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#
# ── WHY IT IS RESOLVED IN A CONTAINER AND NOT IN backend/.venv ──────────────
#
# The venv on the founder's laptop is Python 3.14; the image and CI are 3.13.
# Dependency resolution reads the interpreter version and the platform, so a
# freeze from the laptop can pin versions that will never be installed in
# production and omit ones that will. python:3.13-slim IS the image's base, so
# this is resolved in the place it will be installed.
#
# ── WHAT IT FIXES ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# requirements.txt pins majors: Django==5.2.*, celery==5.4.*. Without this file
# two builds of one commit a week apart could install different code, a
# rollback could not restore a dependency set, and a bad release published
# tonight would be in tomorrow's image with nothing to notice it. Finding 4 of
# docs/SECURITY-AUDIT-2026-09-09.md.
#
# ── WHAT IT DOES NOT FIX, STATED PLAINLY ────────────────────────────────────
#
# There are NO HASHES here. This pins which VERSION is installed, not which
# bytes: it stops an unexpected new release, and it does not verify that the
# artefact PyPI serves for a pinned version is the one that was there before.
# Hashes need `pip install --require-hashes`, which needs a hash for every
# package, which needs pip-tools or an equivalent — a new dependency, and
# Charter 03 §I says one enters only when what is here cannot do the job.
#
# Version pinning does most of the work; say so accurately and do not describe
# this file as supply-chain verification, because it is not that yet.
#
# ── pip IS DELIBERATELY NOT LISTED ──────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The first draft of this file was generated with `pip freeze --all`, which
# reports pip itself, and it was committed with a comment defending that. It
# was wrong: `pip install -r` on a file that pins pip has pip upgrading itself
# mid-install, which is a needless way for a build to fail. The generation
# command above omits --all, and a second independent resolve agreed with this
# file on all 29 real packages once that flag was dropped.
#
